tagline: A leading surface gold tailings retreatment company focused on sustainable operations and value creation in South Africa
hero_kpi_rationale: Gold production volume is the primary operational performance indicator for DRDGOLD, reflecting the company's core activity in extracting and recovering gold from mine tailings. It is a key structural driver of revenue generation.

kpis.name: Gold Production
kpis.explanation: Total quantity of gold produced by the company during the period, expressed in troy ounces.
kpis.description: Gold production decreased by 3.5% to 155,288 ounces (FY2025 vs FY2024 160,818 oz), primarily due to a decline in average grade from 0.225 g/t to 0.189 g/t, partially offset by an increase in throughput from 22.3 to 25.6 million tonnes.
kpis.signal: Slight production decline despite higher throughput

kpis.name: Revenue
kpis.explanation: Total revenue generated from gold sales during the period.
kpis.description: Revenue increased by 33% to ZAR 5,053.2 million (HY2025 vs HY2024 ZAR 3,802.3 million), primarily driven by a 19% (FY2024) and 31% (FY2025) increase in the average rand gold price compared to prior periods.
kpis.signal: Strong revenue growth despite lower production

kpis.name: Operating Profit
kpis.explanation: Profit generated from core operations before taxes and other items.
kpis.description: Operating profit increased by 72% to ZAR 2,712.8 million (HY2025 vs HY2024 ZAR 1,578.7 million), driven by higher gold prices and effective cost management.

kpis.name: Headline Earnings Per Share
kpis.explanation: Adjusted net earnings per share, a measure used in South Africa to reflect ongoing operational performance.
kpis.description: Headline earnings per share nearly doubled to 223.2 ZAR cents (HY2025 vs HY2024 112.6), supported by higher operating profit and a low prior-year base.

kpis.name: Cash Operating Costs
kpis.explanation: Average cost to produce one kilogram of gold in direct cash expenses, including consumables, labor, electricity, and specialized services.
kpis.description: Cash operating costs increased by 13%, rising from ZAR 867,300/kg to ZAR 980,042/kg, pressuring margins despite partial productivity gains from higher throughput.

kpis.name: Average Yield
kpis.explanation: Average amount of gold extracted per tonne of ore or tailings processed.
kpis.description: Average yield declined by 16% (FY2025: 0.189 g/t vs FY2024: 0.225 g/t), primarily due to depletion of higher-grade material from reclamation activities and increased tonnage from lower-grade new recovery sites.
kpis.signal: Significant decline in processed ore quality

kpis.name: Throughput
kpis.explanation: Total volume of ore or mine tailings processed during the period.
kpis.description: Throughput increased by 14.8% to 25.6 million tonnes (FY2025 vs FY2024 22.3 million), partially offsetting the lower average grade and reflecting the commissioning of new recovery sites.

kpis.name: Lost-Time Injury Frequency Rate
kpis.explanation: Number of lost-time injuries per million hours worked, a key safety indicator.
kpis.description: LTIFR increased by 15.7% to 1.33 (vs 1.15 previously), indicating a deterioration in safety conditions requiring focused attention for continuous improvement.

risks.title: Critical dependence on electricity and load shedding in South Africa
risks.score_rationale: Explicitly mentioned in forward-looking statements ("future of power security from South Africa's power utility and intensity of load shedding"). Major operational risk for an energy-intensive mining operation. Direct language indicating strategic concern. Trend increasing in South Africa.

risks.title: Risk of insufficient tailings storage facility capacity
risks.score_rationale: Cited first in forward-looking risks ("regulatory and construction delays in commissioning replacement tailings storage facilities"). Mentioned multiple times (Withok TSF, RTSF). Urgent language ("approach capacity"). Direct impact on medium-term operational viability.

risks.title: Risk of damage to tailings storage facilities
risks.score_rationale: Explicitly listed in forward-looking statements ("damage to tailings storage facilities and excessive maintenance and rehabilitation costs"). Specific risk to mining operations in South Africa. Potentially massive rehabilitation costs mentioned.

risks.title: Gold price volatility and exposure to global markets
risks.score_rationale: Mentioned twice in forward-looking statements ("changes in the demand for and the price of gold", "expected gold price, supply and pricing trends"). Fundamental risk for a gold mining company. Language indicating structural uncertainty.

risks.title: IT disruption and operational cybersecurity risks
risks.score_rationale: Explicitly mentioned ("a disruption in information technology systems, including incidents related to cyber security"). Dedicated Item 16K on cybersecurity. Growing risk for modern mining operations. Direct language but without specific details.

risks.title: Uncertainty regarding mineral reserves and geological assumptions
risks.score_rationale: Mentioned twice ("assumptions underlying our Mineral Reserves... prove to be incorrect", "challenges in replenishing mineral reserves"). Fundamental technical risk for a mining company. Language indicating methodological uncertainty.

risks.title: Dependence on union agreements and social risks
risks.score_rationale: Mentioned in forward-looking statements ("statements with respect to agreements with unions"). South African context with high unionization. Language indicating contractual dependency. Risk of operational disruption.

risks.title: Regulatory risks and loss of operating licenses
risks.score_rationale: Cited in forward-looking statements ("regulatory developments adverse to us or difficulties in maintaining necessary licenses or other governmental approvals"). South African context with strict mining regulation. Language indicating regulatory vulnerability.

ai_positioning.summary: DRDGOLD does not mention any artificial intelligence initiatives in its recent reports. The company focuses on traditional operational optimization, environmental sustainability, and mine tailings management.
evidence: No mention of AI or machine learning technologies in the report
No references to predictive analytics or advanced automation tools
Described innovations are primarily related to tailings processing and environmental compliance
